script.opening_words: You're sitting at your kitchen table on a Tuesday night and you're doing the math again. Not because you want to, because the number in your checking account is doing that thing it does, that thing where it's technically fine but somehow still stressful. Where you make decent money and have nothing obvious to show for it, where you can't point to any single catastrophic decision and yet the financial progress you expected by now just hasn't appeared. You're not
script.ending_words: You don't get a trophy for looking successful. You don't get a medal for the car payment. You know, nobody throws a party when the subscription renews. The system is designed to extract money from you quietly, consistently, in amounts small enough not to trigger alarm and large enough to matter enormously over time. You now know exactly how it works. Um that's the only advantage that was ever available.
script.analysis: Full 44770 canonical characters read. A single-narrator 52-minute numbered-list essay: a kitchen-table hook, the extraction-economy framing, Ramsey and Stanley millionaire research, then 30 habits grouped as big structures (cars, housing, geography, index funds, HSA, match, automation, cards, debt), daily leaks (emergency fund, food, phone, bulk, impulse rule, library, warranties, subscriptions) and income/negotiation habits (lifestyle creep, tracking, salary, insurance, bills, toys, medical bills, taxes, skills, waiting rule), a Housel quotation, a not-too-late message and a 401(k)-match call to action. Most compounding arithmetic reproduces; Direct File advice is out of date, the HSA investing share is understated, and several survey figures are dated or unsourced.
beat_map: Habits 7-12: investing, HSA, match, automation, cards, debt.
Midpoint: from big structures to daily leaks.
Habits 21-30: lifestyle creep, negotiation, medical bills, taxes, skills, waiting rule.
Call to action: check the 401(k) match tonight.

topic.analysis: Thirty unglamorous saving, investing and negotiating habits, each converted into a compounded dollar figure.
topic.audience_problem: Decent earners who feel stuck and cannot see where their money goes.
topic.time_sensitivity: Low to medium: contribution limits, tax-filing options and survey figures update annually.
topic.narrative_angle: Wealth is invisible and boring; the extraction economy profits from people who do not know the math.
topic.novelty_and_corpus_angle: Test an original long habit list that keeps the compounding conversions and a single concrete call to action, but updates year-specific limits and tax-filing options and sources each survey figure.
topic.competition: Same-channel nearest-age peers in K01; not an independent niche or causal test
